title: Lope de Soria (Mirandola) to Charles V, 13 Dec 1527, RAH Salazar 9/17 ff. 31-34 (DECODE R9487, dated there 1517)

documents.shelfmark: RAH, Colección Salazar y Castro, 9/17, ff. 31-34 (DECODE R9487)
documents.route: Lope de Soria (imperial agent, Mirandola) to Charles V

plaintext.source: contemporary decipherment 'Claro' A-C bound as f. 34r; torn in B and C

transcription.source: not transcribed sign by sign; DECODE images viewed, decipherment transcribed (claro.md)
transcription.notes: About 25 cipher lines on ff. 31r-33r, torn at the right edges.

system.summary: Soria's key B (1523): homophonic letters plus three-letter code groups (zog=de, zof=con, xab=Francia, sub=que); Spanish.
system.notes: Same key as soria1523 key B, so in use by 1527.

prior_solution.where: contemporary decipherment bound as f. 34r of the same letter

conditions.human_role: Project-level: obtained a DECODE login with privileges and passed its session cookie to the model, set up Claude Code with Opus 5, and posed the problem with /goal. No target-specific intervention recorded.

solution.what: Fetched the 4 DECODE images of R9487 with the shared cookie.
Recognised the three-letter code groups (xip, yed, zog, sub, pic) as Soria's 1523 key B from soria1523.
Viewed every page: f. 34r is headed 'Claro' with sections A, B, C in a secretary's hand, docketed 'xiij de deziembre [1]527'.
Key-B values on the f. 33r cipher give 'matrimonio con Francia', 'por no', 'navegar con', and on f. 31r 'quitanças de', all in the claro.
Redated the letter to 1527 from its content (Genoa lost, Pope at Orvieto, Leyva at Milan, Bourbon's jewels) and the docket.

outcome.method_basis: The court's decipherment ('Claro', sections A-C) is bound as f. 34r of the same letter; spot checks with Soria's 1523 key B from the sibling target soria1523 confirmed it matches the cipher.
outcome.notes: Read at the time; decipherment f. 34r (torn in B/C). DECODE date 1517 corrected to 1527. Catalogue entry 142 removed; no write-up.
